chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about stagnant water and cleansing oneself from it, so he said: “Perform wudu (ablution) from the other side, and do not perform wudu (ablution) from the side of the carcass.”

key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الْآخَرِ: the opposite side, away from the source of contamination
key_terms.الْجِيفَةِ: the carcass or dead animal body
key_terms.الْمَاءِ السَّاكِنِ: stagnant water that is not flowing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) from stagnant water when a carcass is in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the use of stagnant water when a carcass is present in or near it. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that wudu (ablution) may be taken from the opposite side, but not from the side of the carcass, indicating caution regarding impurity and contamination in matters of taharah.
